REGULAR MEETING AGENDA
CITY COUNCIL OF THE CITY OF CERRITOS
AND THE SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY
THURSDAY - JULY 25, 2019 - CITY HALL -
07:00 P.M.
City Council Chamber
AGENDA MATERIALS: Reports and materials related to items on this Agenda are available for public inspection at the City Clerk's Office, Cerritos City Hall, 18125 Bloomfield Avenue, Cerritos, CA 90703, during normal business hours, 8 a.m. to 5 p.m., Monday through Friday, Telephone (562) 916-1248. Materials submitted to the City Council/Successor Agency after distribution of the agenda packet are available for public inspection in the City Clerk's Office at the above address during normal business hours as noted.
PUBLIC COMMENTS: For all Agenda Items, except for Consent Calendar Items, public comments will be allowed at the time each matter comes up for discussion. Please complete and submit a blue Speaker's Card to ensure that you are recognized when the Agenda item is considered. The general public comments portion of the meeting, under Agenda Item 6, will not exceed 45 minutes, and no speaker will be allowed more than five minutes, unless determined appropriate by the Chair. To assist in the preparation of appropriate responses, persons are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record.
PUBLIC HEARINGS: Public hearings will be conducted in the order indicated on the agenda, unless otherwise directed. Please complete and submit a blue Speakers Card if you wish to present testimony. Conduct of public hearings will occur in substantially the following sequence: the item to be heard is announced, a report of written correspondence and staff report are received, and the City Council asks questions of staff. The public hearing is opened and verbal testimony will occur in the following order: the applicant, if applicable, those in favor, opposed, or interested parties, and rebuttal by applicant. Speakers are requested, but not required, to state their name and city of residence for the record. After verbal testimony, the public hearing is closed and the matter is deliberated with a determination being made or a continuation of the matter.

Items under the Consent Calendar are considered routine and will be enacted by one motion. City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings
During this part of the meeting members of the City Council report to the community on various matters of interest, including reports concerning committees on which the Councilmembers serve and reports on meetings/conferences attended. In addition, requests may be made of the staff for reports which will be presented to the City Council at a subsequent meeting, or for the scheduling of future agenda items. There will be no discussion or action taken on any of the items that may be presented during this agenda item.
12.

MINUTES OF A REGULAR MEETING OF THE CERRITOS CITY COUNCIL AND THE
SUCCESSOR AGENCY TO THE CERRITOS REDEVELOPMENT AGENCY HELD ON JULY
25, 2019, IN THE COUNCIL CHAMBER AT CERRITOS CITY HALL, 18125
BLOOMFIELD AVENUE, CERRITOS, CALIFORNIA

1.  Call to Order

  The meeting was called to order at 7:00 p.m.

2.  Invocation

  The invocation was given by City Clerk Vida Barone.

3.  Pledge of Allegiance

  The Pledge of Allegiance was led by Cerritos Recreation Services Youth Soccer
  League Pee Wee Team, “Lightning.”

4.  Roll Call

  The following members of the City Council/Successor Agency were in attendance:

  Council/Agency Member Jim Edwards
  Council/Agency Member Grace Hu
  Council/Agency Member Mark E. Pulido
  Mayor Pro Tem/Vice Chair Frank A. Yokoyama
  Mayor/Chair Naresh Solanki

5.  Presentations/Appointments

5A.  Presentations

  A Proclamation was made as follows:

  G3 – Quality (Business Spotlight).

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions

  Linda Grace expressed concern regarding excessive truck noise on Bloomfield
  Avenue.

  Faye Ashby expressed concern regarding excessive truck noise on Bloomfield
  Avenue.

  Charles Jordan expressed concern regarding excessive truck noise on Bloomfield
  Avenue.

  Chris Aafedt expressed concern regarding excessive truck noise on Bloomfield
  Avenue and requested an item be placed on the next agenda to remove
  Bloomfield Avenue as a truck route.

  CW van der Linden inquired whether CalTrans was “back billing” Cerritos for street
  tarring work.

  Gigi Meese, Director of Community Relations 3D Theatricals, invited the community
  to the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts production of "Shrek: The Musical"
  and other upcoming performances.

  Kathie Welch requested a variance on the house paint color palette approved for
  City residences.
 City of Cerritos  July 25, 2019

6.  Public Comments and Suggestions (continued)

  Jay Gray expressed concern regarding the potential reduction of public comment
  time limits and the City Treasurer position.

  Kirit Chavhan requested as assessment study as to the structure and requirements
  for residential chimneys and roofs in the City, particularly as related to earthquake
  preparedness.

  John Darnell requested closure of the cul-de-sacs in Neighborhood Watch Zone 59
  and submitted a document for the record.

  Schyler Barnes-Anaya requested closure of the cul-de-sacs in Neighborhood Watch
  Zone 59.

  Artellia Johnson requested transparency into the public process, particularly as
  related to the leasing of the Mullikin building by the City.

  Murali Vasudevan requested transparency into the public process, expressed
  concerns with pine trees and reduction in public comment time limits, and the
  status of pending projects such as the online parking permit system.

  Sam Desai requested a report regarding the US Conference of Mayors conference,
  inquired as to the City’s business license process, City opportunities for arts and
  crafts vendors, appointment of the City Treasurer, and a fundraiser for the CCPA.

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9.  New and Old Business

9A.  Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1364-19, Construction of asphalt
  improvements in City of Cerritos parking lot, Project No. 19441 (COUNCIL).

  Staff reports were given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer and Kristin
  Aguila, Advance Planning Manager. A PowerPoint presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract for Bid No. 1364-19, in the amount of $1,348,584 for
  construction of Asphalt Improvements in City of Cerritos Parking Lot, Project No.
  19441, to Shawnan and reject all other bids; and

  2. Amend the contract to American Engineering in the amount of $66,563 for the
  construction administration, inspection, and material testing services for Phase
  2 of the project; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki
  NOES:  None
  ABSENT:  None
  ABSTAIN:  None

9B.  Review and consideration of award of bids for Project No. 20302: Bid No. 1371-
  19, Construction of tree improvements on 183rd Street and Bid No. 1372-19,
  Construction of concrete improvements on 183rd Street (COUNCIL).

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint
  presentation was displayed.

  The Mayor opened public comments. Noting there were no individuals who elected
  to speak, the Mayor closed public comments.

  MOTION: It was moved by Hu, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Reject the sole bid for Bid No. 1371-19, for the complete removal of the 19
  parkway trees (total bid), Project No. 20302, from Mariposa Landscape; and

  2. Award a contract for Bid No. 1372-19, in the amount of $59,910 for
  Construction of Concrete Improvements on 183rd Street (base bid plus
  Alternate #1), Project No. 20302, to Ruiz Concrete & Paving and reject the other
  bids; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

9C.  Review and consideration of award of Bid No. 1373-19, Construction of roofing

  A staff report was given by Dario Simoes, Assistant City Engineer. A PowerPoint

  MOTION: It was moved by Yokoyama, and seconded by Edwards, to:

  1. Award a contract for Bid No. 1373-19 in the amount of $198,020 for Cerritos

  2. Amend the contract to Larsen Zienkiewicz in the amount of $14,000 for
  construction administration of the project; and

  3. Authorize the City Manager or his designee to execute any project-related
  change orders (COUNCIL).

  The motion carried (5 - 0) as follows:

  AYES:  Edwards, Hu, Pulido, Yokoyama, Solanki

11.  City Council Communications/Committee Reports/Report on Meetings

  Reports were provided by Councilmembers Pulido, Yokoyama, and Edwards,
  Mayor Pro Tem Yokoyama and Mayor Solanki.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Direct staff to return a report to the City Council
  related to the potential of prohibiting the sale of vaping products throughout the
  City.

  CONSENSUS (Yokoyama): Direct staff to return a report to the City Council
  related to the effectiveness of the adopted ordinances prohibiting the licensing of
  marijuana in the City.

  CONSENSUS (Hu): Direct staff to place a report on the August 22, 2019 agenda
  regarding operation of the Cerritos Center for the Performing Arts.
